clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old immunocompetent male from a Fasciola-endemic area presented to the emergency department with a 7-day history of dull right hypochondriac pain and intermittent low-grade fever. On admission, he was hypotensive (90/60 mmHg) with mild right upper quadrant tenderness on examination, but no peritoneal signs or jaundice. Laboratory studies revealed leukocytosis (12.3 G/L with 75.3% neutrophils), elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 79.8 mg/dL, fibrinogen 6.88 g/L), but normal liver enzymes and bilirubin. Ultrasound imaging identified a poorly demarcated heterogeneous lesion in liver segment BE with central hypoechoic liquefied necrotic areas consistent with an abscess. CT imaging revealed an abnormal high attenuation linear structure within the lesion, suspected to be a foreign body, with no intra- or extraperitoneal gas or fluid, ruling out gastrointestinal perforation. Surgical exploration confirmed a 3 cm fishbone embedded within the liver abscess, with intraoperative inspection showing no evidence of gastric or duodenal perforation. Blood culture was positive for Streptococcus gordonii, while surgical abscess drainage culture was negative. Postoperatively, the patient had resolution of fever, and inflammatory markers gradually decreased, with complete clinical resolution achieved within one week.
